title: Assembly Quick Reference
description: Look up a lesson idea, see its small example, and check a common mistake. Open the linked lesson for setup and practice steps.

entries.name: Return a small result
entries.summary: rdi is a register: a tiny storage place in the processor. Linux exit reads its status from rdi.

example.code:
global _start
section .text
_start:
    mov rdi, 5
    mov rax, 60
    syscall

notes: Exit codes are only 0 to 255; use small values in these lessons.

entries.name: Copy a register value
entries.summary: mov copies a value. It does not erase the source register.

example.code:
global _start
section .text
_start:
    mov rbx, 3
    mov rdi, rbx
    mov rax, 60
    syscall

notes: The destination comes first in NASM syntax.

entries.name: Add two numbers
entries.summary: add changes its first register by adding the second value.

example.code:
global _start
section .text
_start:
    mov rdi, 3
    add rdi, 2
    mov rax, 60
    syscall

notes: The add instruction changes the destination register.

entries.name: Subtract a number
entries.summary: sub subtracts the second value from the first register.

example.code:
global _start
section .text
_start:
    mov rdi, 8
    sub rdi, 3
    mov rax, 60
    syscall

notes: Keep the result within a small positive range for exit codes.

entries.name: Multiply a value
entries.summary: imul multiplies signed integers. This form stores the result in its first register.

example.code:
global _start
section .text
_start:
    mov rdi, 3
    imul rdi, rdi, 2
    mov rax, 60
    syscall

notes: Large results can overflow a register.

entries.name: Divide a whole number
entries.summary: div divides rdx:rax by its input. For this small positive example, clear rdx first.

example.code:
global _start
section .text
_start:
    mov rax, 8
    xor rdx, rdx
    mov rbx, 3
    div rbx
    mov rdi, rax
    mov rax, 60
    syscall

notes: Never divide by zero. The remainder is in rdx, not rax.

entries.name: Keep chosen bits
entries.summary: and keeps only bits that are 1 in both inputs. A final bit of 1 marks an odd number.

example.code:
global _start
section .text
_start:
    mov rdi, 5
    and rdi, 1
    mov rax, 60
    syscall

notes: Bitwise and is an operation on bits, not a high-level if statement.

entries.name: Choose a path
entries.summary: cmp compares values and sets flags. je jumps when the compared values are equal.

example.code:
global _start
section .text
_start:
    mov rdi, 0
    mov rbx, 5
    cmp rbx, 5
    je .same
    jmp .done
.same:
    mov rdi, 1
.done:
    mov rax, 60
    syscall

notes: A jump uses flags from the previous comparison; avoid changing them first.

entries.name: Repeat with a counter
entries.summary: A label names a place in the code. jnz repeats while the last result was not zero.

example.code:
global _start
section .text
_start:
    mov rcx, 3
    mov rdi, 0
.again:
    add rdi, 2
    dec rcx
    jnz .again
    mov rax, 60
    syscall

notes: A loop needs a counter or rule that eventually stops.

entries.name: Save and restore a value
entries.summary: push places a value on the stack. pop takes the most recent value back.

example.code:
global _start
section .text
_start:
    push 7
    pop rdi
    mov rax, 60
    syscall

entries.name: Call a small routine
entries.summary: call saves a return address and jumps. ret returns to the instruction after call.

example.code:
global _start
section .text
_start:
    mov rdi, 4
    call twice
    mov rax, 60
    syscall
twice:
    add rdi, rdi
    ret

notes: A routine reached by call should return with ret, not fall into unrelated code.

entries.name: Ask Linux to write text
entries.summary: The write system call uses rax=1, rdi=1 for standard output, an address in rsi and a length in rdx.

example.code:
global _start
section .data
message: db "Hi", 10
section .text
_start:
    mov rax, 1
    mov rdi, 1
    lea rsi, [rel message]
    mov rdx, 3
    syscall
    mov rdi, 0
    mov rax, 60
    syscall

notes: The length counts bytes, including the newline byte.
